subject: Renewal + capacity bump — usage floor & credit cushion proposal
messages:
From: Eliza Norton <eliza@verdant.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 12 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal + expected capacity increase — pricing questions

Hi Tessa,

Hope you’re well. We’ve been reviewing usage ahead of our October renewal and expect a 30-40% step-up in inference volume over the next 12 months as we roll the new assistant to more customers. Before we finalize the PO, two asks from procurement and engineering that I want to confirm: 1) can Redwood hold current unit pricing for the first 90 days of the new term while we ramp (a short price freeze), and 2) can we get a small pool of burst credits or a usage-floor arrangement so surges during rollout don’t push us over our budget?

We’re evaluating a 12-month renewal with a modest increase in committed tokens if that opens up a better rate. Marco (cc’d) will manage the procurement paperwork.

Can you send options (commit levels, credits, and any pro-rata terms)? We need an internal proposal to share with finance by Sep 18.

Thanks,
Eliza
Eliza Norton
Head of Platform — Verdant AI
eliza@verdant.ai

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
To: Eliza Norton <eliza@verdant.ai>, Marco Diaz <marco@verdant.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal + expected capacity increase — pricing questions

Eliza — thanks for the heads up and for the ramp expectations. I put together three concise options so Verdant can pick the operational tradeoff that fits the ramp. Attachment: pricing_summary_v3.xlsx (summary + line items).

Option A — Short-term protection (best for rapid ramp)- 12-month renewal, current unit rates frozen for the first 90 days (price freeze)- No change to base commit; we add a 10% burst credit pool (applied to overage at $0 until credits exhausted)- True-up at quarter end; standard overage rates resume after day 91

Option B — Moderate commit uplift (best price for committed growth)- 12-month renewal with 25% increase to committed monthly tokens- 12% discount on unit price vs. current list (applies from day 1)- 5% supplemental burst credits + 45-day price freeze window

Option C — Higher-commit anchor (best long-term unit economics)- 12-month renewal with 40% commit increase- 20% discount on unit price- 3 months of burst credits equal to 8% of annual committed tokens- Contract includes an invoice true-up cadence and a capped overage rate

Notes and operational points- We can prorate the initial term and align invoicing to your fiscal quarter if helpful.- All options include automatic prefix caching and a recommended batch profile to optimize cost during surge windows — engineering can help tune during rollout.- If you prefer a multi-year term we can extend discounts but I kept this to 12 months since you mentioned a near-term ramp.

If you want, I can route Option B to Finance for a small concession (discount extension or an additional credit tranche) — looping Ben for visibility and quick approval. Final pricing sheet attached.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
(415) 555-0189

From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Verdant AI renewal — recommend Option B with small concession

Ben / Karthik — forwarding Verdant’s ask and the options I sent. Quick ask: Eliza is leaning toward Option B (25% commit uplift + 12% discount + 45-day freeze). They asked if we can add one more 2% credit tranche (effectively a small goodwill buffer) if we agree to the 12% discount. That would be ~2% of annual committed tokens in credits (one-off).

Rationale:- Upsell opportunity: higher committed volume improves predictability and moves them from pay-as-you-go to a meaningful commit.- Short-term operational risk: the 45-day freeze + credits reduces lift-failure friction during their rollout.- Competitive context: they have a competing renewal offer from a hyperscaler that includes a short-term price concession.

If we approve the extra 2% credit tranche I’ll include it in the renewal amendment and route the PDF for signature. Need an OK or alternate suggestion by EOD tomorrow (Sep 16) to meet their procurement timeline.

Thanks,
Tessa

---
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Verdant AI renewal — recommend Option B with small concession

Tessa — I support Option B with the concession but propose one guardrail: make the 2% credit tranche conditional on a signed amendment and an agreed telemetry checkpoint at 45 days (engineering check to confirm the prefix cache and batch tuning reduced per-token cost as expected). If telemetry shows <10% reduction in projected overage risk, credits vest; otherwise we hold the tranche until the next billing quarter.

Also, add a short clause that if monthly consumption exceeds 150% of the committed tokens for two consecutive months, overage rate reverts to the higher tier (we should be clear on runaway risk).

Ben — can you confirm finance is good with the 12% discount + conditional 2% credit? If yes, Tessa can finalize the amendment.

Karthik
VP, Revenue Operations — Redwood Inference
